answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a bonded vertex graph: each agent identity is one vertex whose edge weight comes from a locked, slashable deposit plus a cipher proof tying its actions to one keypair over time. Like water carving karst, cheap identities erode: minting thousands of vertices multiplies the locked, forfeitable stake, so an attacker pays linearly per fake identity while an honest agent pays once. Trade-off: newcomers face a deposit barrier, so the bond should be small, time-decaying, and refundable after clean history.
